subject: Welcome to the Competition
body: Access credentials to the competition environment will follow in the next inject. Reply to confirm: (1) your team is ready to compete, (2) all workstations are functional with enough seats for each competitor, (3) you have received and agree to abide by the rules in the team packet, and (4) you will refer to your team only by number, never by organization name, when communicating with judges or White Team. All team communication with White Team must go through the inject/scoring system; a voice or chat channel may also be provided, but assume it is not private.

subject: Environment Access Credentials
body: Your environment is available at the address provided in the team portal. Initial account credentials have been issued to your team; change all initial passwords immediately upon first login. Note that VM reverts/snapshots are a limited resource and may incur a scoring penalty - request them only through the designated technical support inject. Close unused sessions to preserve environment performance. Contact competition management directly if a request goes unanswered for more than 20 minutes.

subject: Scoring Inquiries
body: Use this channel to ask why a service is not scoring as expected. Responses are at the discretion of the scoring manager and will arrive as a notification. Teams remain responsible for diagnosing and correcting the underlying cause of any scoring failure; an external workstation is provided outside your perimeter to help you verify service availability from an attacker's-eye view.

subject: Password Change Notification Procedure
body: Password changes are an expected part of good security hygiene, but excessive or unbatched changes create scoring overhead. Submit password changes that affect scored services through this notification channel, one account per notification, batched no more than once per scoring period. Administrator and root-level accounts are never used for scoring, so those may be changed freely without notifying White Team.

subject: Incident Reporting
body: If you suspect Red Team activity, submit an Incident Report with as much detail as possible - one report per incident. Thorough, timely reporting can recover a portion of points lost to successful attacks. Include: date/time attack started (if known), date/time discovered, attacker source address, target system and port/service, attack type, result of the attack, the vulnerability that allowed it, how it was discovered, how it was contained, remediation actions taken, and the result of remediation.

subject: Technical Support and Environment Revert Requests
body: Use this channel only for faults with the underlying environment (a VM that fails to boot or hangs indefinitely) - not for problems you are expected to fix as part of the competition. You may request a full or partial revert/scrub of a system to its original state; be specific about which system, understand this may take up to 20 minutes and typically carries a scoring penalty, and do not submit duplicate requests for the same revert. You will need to power the system back on once the revert completes.

subject: Inject Response Format Standard
body: Respond to all injects using a professional business-memo format (Word or PDF preferred), addressing the stated recipient role and following each inject's specific deliverable instructions. Include screenshots wherever the inject calls for validation of a completed task. Always refer to your team by number only - never by real name or organization - in any written response.

subject: Competition Feedback Survey
body: Each member of your team is asked to complete the post-competition feedback survey linked in the team portal. Your input directly shapes future events - please respond before the closing ceremony.

subject: Outbound Access Exception Request
body: A content filter restricts outbound web access from the competition environment to an approved list. If a legitimate business task is blocked by this filter (for example, a vendor documentation site), submit a request here describing the site and the business justification. Approval is at White Team's discretion and any change will be confirmed via notification.

subject: Compliance Scorecard Review
body: As you complete injects that map to specific compliance controls, log them on the compliance scorecard included in your team packet. Auditors will review this scorecard near the end of the competition and may ask you to demonstrate any control you have marked complete, so keep supporting evidence on hand.

subject: Asset and Service Inventory
body: Prior documentation of our environment is out of date and incomplete, which makes it difficult to plan resource allocation or respond to audits. Produce an inventory covering every device in your environment with, at minimum: system name, purpose, OS and version, IP address(es), critical applications, a list of admin/user/service accounts, running services, and open ports (use a scanning tool such as Nmap to verify). Keep this document current for the remainder of the competition - you will be audited against it on short notice.

subject: Baseline Configuration Documentation
body: Establish and document baseline configurations for each system, including installed software with version and patch level, running services, current user accounts, and OS/patch level. Baselines should reflect the current state of the environment and will be used later in the competition to detect unauthorized change.

subject: Detailed Inventory Validation Scan
body: Auditors require independent validation of your previously submitted asset inventory. Run a detailed scan of every device to confirm system name, OS version, IP address(es), and open ports with associated services, and separately run a local account audit to confirm account name, type, and last login for every host. Submit both as a clearly labeled appendix, distinct from your original manually-reported inventory, along with screenshots of the tools used.
deliverable_format: business memo with tabular validation data (docx/pdf)

subject: Team Organization Chart
body: Provide an organization chart and short memo identifying team positions (not individuals) - such as Firewall Lead or Linux Administrator - along with the skill set each role requires. Note how leadership and inject-completion coordination is handled, whether each position has adequate backup coverage, and where you assess skill gaps in your current staffing.

subject: Acceptable Use Policy
body: Draft an Acceptable Use Policy ready for employees to sign, covering at minimum: email, internet usage, social media and blogging, mobile devices and IoT, personal use of company equipment, and personal digital assistants in the workplace. Ensure it does not conflict with existing policy or law, and give proper credit if outside sources are used in drafting.

subject: Sensitive Data Handling Policy
body: Following a peer company's breach and subsequent legal exposure, draft a formal policy governing the appropriate use, protection, and disposal of sensitive, proprietary, and personally identifiable information in all forms (paper, media, backups, cloud, phone). At minimum define: the policy's authority and effective date, who is subject to it, what qualifies as sensitive information with examples, covered media, protection mechanisms (labeling, encryption, secure disposal, contractual controls), training requirements, and consequences for non-compliance. Separately, recommend technical mechanisms to identify, classify, and protect this information going forward.

subject: Data Retention and eDiscovery Readiness
body: A potential lawsuit requires us to be ready to produce records on short notice. Prepare: a list of systems and where their major data lives (documents, shared folders, home directories, mailboxes, log stores), a capture of relevant outbound traffic logs for the window specified by counsel, any relevant call or communication logs, and a proposed data retention policy going forward.
deliverable_format: business memo with supporting log excerpts

subject: Response to Legal Records Request
body: We have received a formal request to produce system logs for a specified time window in plain-text format. Ensure the produced file is appropriately labeled with a data classification marking so it is protected from broader public disclosure.

subject: Incident Response Plan
body: Develop an incident handling policy that addresses initial containment, notification obligations, evidence collection to determine how/when/what was breached, and criteria for involving law enforcement. Base your plan on recognized incident-handling guidance and note it should be treated as adopted by your team, not a draft.

subject: Incident Response Plan - External Communications Update
body: Legal and audit review of your existing incident response plan found a gap: it lacks guidance on communicating an incident to media, law enforcement, internet service providers, partners, and customers. Add a subsection addressing, for each of these five audiences: who is authorized to speak with them and what approval is required, when communication should occur, what details may be shared, what channels are used, and what preparation/training supports this. Submit the updated policy with additions visibly distinguished (e.g. a different font color) from the original.
deliverable_format: updated policy document with tracked additions

subject: Physical Security Procedures
body: Document your physical security policy and the procedures you have implemented for visitors and non-employee personnel accessing your workspace, including how sensitive information is protected from casual observation.

subject: Disaster Recovery Plan
body: Auditors have noted we lack a formal plan for outages and other catastrophic events. Outline the elements of an effective plan that protects against data loss and enables rapid recovery given our existing hardware, and identify what tools, products, or procedures are needed to implement it.

subject: Staff Development and Skills Gap Assessment
body: As part of budget planning for staff development, review the skills present on your team and identify where additional training would improve performance. Be specific about which roles or skill areas need reinforcement.

subject: Tools and Technology Inventory
body: Provide an inventory of the tools your team uses regularly to manage and secure the environment, with a brief description of each tool's function and benefit.

subject: Security Control Framework Mapping
body: Map how your environment currently addresses each control area in the assigned security control framework (e.g. the CIS Critical Security Controls, or NIST 800-171 if this is a compliance-themed event). Produce a document with one heading per control area and a short paragraph describing how it is addressed in your environment today.

subject: Unauthorized Use Detection Procedure
body: Develop a written procedure and implementation policy to identify, detect, and report unauthorized use of organizational systems. Include an example of the reporting mechanism's output.

subject: Firewall Policy Alignment Review
body: Review your firewall policies against your submitted asset inventory to confirm every rule maps to a legitimate, expected service. Document each policy statement and the service or service combination it permits, with screenshots validating the configuration, and describe any additional firewall features you have enabled.

subject: Application-Layer Firewall Policy
body: Develop firewall policy that leverages application-layer identification rather than plain transport-protocol and port matching wherever the platform supports it. Policy should permit scored services, restrict outbound traffic to expected responses plus legitimate internal needs, appropriately segment traffic between network zones, deny everything else by default, and enable threat protection on all permitted flows. Document each policy statement and whether it governs inbound, outbound, or default-deny traffic, with a screenshot of the rule base.

subject: Denial-of-Service Protection Policy
body: Recent industry reporting highlights the frequency of denial-of-service attacks against organizations like ours. Configure your perimeter firewall with a DoS protection policy and zone protection on the external-facing zone. Report how this was accomplished with screenshots of the policy and the zone protection settings.

subject: Best-Practice Security Profiles
body: Most malware reaches networks through otherwise-legitimate applications, so all permitted traffic needs threat inspection. Attach best-practice security profiles - antivirus, vulnerability protection, anti-spyware, URL filtering, file blocking, and sandboxed file detonation where available - to every rule that allows traffic on your internet gateway, then group them into a reusable profile group. Provide screenshots of each profile and confirmation that the profile group is applied fleet-wide.

subject: Enable Intrusion Prevention / Threat Protection
body: Enable the intrusion-prevention or threat-protection capability of your perimeter firewall and apply it to both inbound and outbound policies. Document how this was accomplished with a screenshot of the policy showing the feature enabled, and a screenshot of the threat log showing at least one detected event.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and log screenshots

subject: Restrict Access to Non-Business Websites
body: Employees are spending time on sites unrelated to day-to-day operations. Configure URL category or custom URL blocking to restrict end-user access to major social media sites. Document the configuration and provide monitor-log examples showing the firewall successfully blocking the traffic. This is needed ahead of an upcoming leadership review.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and log screenshots

subject: Departmental Exception to URL Blocking
body: Following the recent social-media block, Marketing has reported they can no longer engage customers online. Create a URL category and policy exception that restores access to select social media platforms only for members of the Marketing group, while all other users remain blocked. Document the configuration and provide evidence that the exception applies correctly to Marketing but not to other users.

subject: Data Loss Prevention Policy
body: A recent third-party breach may have exposed sensitive account information of ours. The Board now requires that private or confidential data leaving the network be monitored and, where possible, blocked. Define a data-filtering policy on the perimeter firewall that flags or blocks outbound transmission of documents matching sensitive-data patterns (e.g. a confidentiality marker, or common PII patterns such as SSNs/credit card numbers). Document the configuration with screenshots.

subject: Quality of Service Marking
body: Traffic to and from our public-facing servers needs consistent priority treatment. Implement a QoS/marking policy (e.g. DSCP or IP precedence) on the firewall or router so that traffic to designated servers receives preferential handling, while other traffic is left at default priority. Validate with a packet capture showing correct marking, and document the configuration commands or screens used.

subject: Screening Router Hardening
body: Configure the border/head-end router with access lists (or zone-based equivalent) to screen unnecessary services and clearly invalid packets (fragmented, abnormally low TTL) before they reach the internal firewall. Also harden the router itself: remove unneeded services, secure management access, and check for unexpected files in local storage. Document the relevant configuration commands.
deliverable_format: business memo with CLI configuration excerpts

subject: Captive Web Portal for Internet Access
body: Implement a captive web portal on the perimeter firewall so that only authenticated users are permitted outbound internet access. Document the implementation and provide a screenshot of the captive portal splash page as seen from an internal client attempting to reach the internet.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and portal screenshots

subject: SSL/TLS Decryption for Outbound Inspection
body: Enable forward-proxy SSL/TLS decryption on the perimeter firewall so outbound encrypted traffic can be inspected for threats. Generate and deploy the certificates needed to establish the firewall as a trusted intermediary, including distribution of the forward-trust certificate to client trust stores. Provide a screenshot of the traffic log showing at least one session successfully decrypted.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and log screenshots

subject: Scheduled Firewall Configuration Backup
body: Configure the perimeter firewall to perform an automatic daily configuration backup to a designated internal server, at a time of your choosing. Provide a screenshot of the backup configuration and evidence that a test backup completed successfully.

subject: Remote Access VPN for Support Staff
body: Industry practice for remote administrative access is a client VPN rather than direct exposure of internal management interfaces. Configure a remote-access VPN service on the perimeter firewall compatible with a standard VPN client, with user authentication against Active Directory or local credentials. Document the configuration end-to-end with screenshots.

subject: Defend Against Firewall Rule Enumeration
body: There are indications attackers are attempting to map our firewall ruleset using packet-TTL-based enumeration techniques. Modify router or firewall access lists to drop packets with inappropriate TTL values that indicate this kind of probing. Document the relevant configuration commands and where the list is applied.
deliverable_format: business memo with CLI configuration excerpts

subject: Centralized Logging Implementation
body: Policy requires a centralized logging service, which we currently lack. Stand up a logging solution and configure every networked device - including the perimeter firewall - to forward logs to it. Document your installation with a screenshot of the console/GUI, screenshots of the forwarding configuration on each device, a sample of composite logs showing multiple sources reporting in, and evidence that the logging server's clock is synchronized with the rest of the environment.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and log screenshots

subject: Evaluate Alternate Centralized Logging Solution
body: Evaluate an alternate open-source centralized-logging technology against your current solution. Summarize the pros and cons of each, and provide a recommendation as to whether the organization should migrate.

subject: Network Time Synchronization
body: Consistent time across the network is essential for usable logs and incident timelines. Designate a single authoritative time source and configure every server, workstation, and network device to synchronize to it. Provide screenshots demonstrating synchronized time across each device type, along with the commands or utilities used.

subject: Consistent Login/Warning Banners
body: Best practice requires that login banners not disclose system or version information, since that information significantly increases attractiveness as an attack target. Every banner should instead state: authorized users only, access is monitored, use constitutes consent to monitoring, and logs may be used to prosecute abuse. Implement this banner across every network device, system, and server prior to login (e.g. SSH, RDP). Provide an inventory of where it was implemented with a screenshot of each banner appearing before the login prompt.

subject: Network Traffic Baseline
body: Establish a network-traffic baseline to inform bandwidth planning. Produce a table of every host and its average transmit/receive traffic volume, using your firewall, centralized logging, or native OS tools (or a combination). Document how the data was gathered with example screenshots.
deliverable_format: business memo with traffic table and screenshots

subject: Top Attacker Source Report
body: Leadership needs a report on the top 10 source IP addresses attacking the organization over the past 24 hours, using your firewall's threat monitoring feature. This is needed quickly - please complete within the timeframe specified.

subject: Top Threat Category Report
body: Produce a report of the top 10 threat categories observed over the past 24 hours using your firewall's threat summary data, including how many times each was seen. For each, assess whether it warrants further action: is it reportable, does it reveal a gap in current protections, or does it indicate an existing control is working as intended?

subject: DNS Traffic Monitoring
body: Provide a screenshot from your firewall's traffic monitor filtered to show only DNS traffic destined for the internal DNS server, so leadership can confirm the service is being watched.

subject: Application Usage Trend Report
body: Produce a report showing how the mix of application usage on the network has changed over the last several hours, using your firewall's application visibility features. Include the underlying chart or data in your memo.

subject: Abnormal Activity Log Review
body: Using your central log repository, identify log entries that appear to represent an attack or Red Team activity. Provide screenshots of those entries along with your reasoning for why each is suspicious.

subject: Suspicious Traffic Packet Capture
body: Using a packet-capture tool from a vantage point outside your perimeter, capture a filtered set of packets that you believe represents Red Team activity. Submit the filtered capture with a written explanation of why you believe this traffic is malicious.

subject: Enable User Identification on the Firewall
body: To enforce policy based on Active Directory groups or individual users rather than IP address alone, enable the firewall's user-identification feature (agent-based or agentless) so it can map network traffic to authenticated users and their AD group memberships. Confirm and include output from a CLI command that shows active user-to-IP mappings.
deliverable_format: business memo with configuration and CLI output

subject: Internal Vulnerability Scan
body: Run an internal vulnerability scan of all in-scope systems using an open-source or commercial scanner. Document open ports and known vulnerabilities by host, along with your remediation plan, presented in tabular form. Provide screenshots of the scanner running against each host.
deliverable_format: business memo with tabular findings and screenshots

subject: External Vulnerability Scan
body: From a system on the external/public segment, scan your organization's external address range. Document what tool(s) you used with screenshots, produce a table of open ports by IP address, and add any known vulnerabilities the tool identifies for each entry.
deliverable_format: business memo with tabular findings and screenshots

subject: Internal Network Port and Service Discovery
body: Multiple industry breaches have started with servers or services unintentionally exposed due to firewall misconfiguration. From inside your perimeter, scan every network segment and device under your control (including all TCP ports and the common UDP services such as DNS, SNMP, and Windows RPC). Submit the full scan results as an appendix and a memo describing what you scanned, an executive summary of the findings (expected vs. unexpected exposure), and recommended next steps.

subject: OS and Firmware Patch-Level Review
body: Evaluate the OS version and patch level of every server, workstation, and network device. Document current versions, the recommended version/patch level for each, and whether you have already remediated any gaps found since the competition began.

subject: Known Vulnerability (CVE) Review
body: Cross-reference the OS and firmware release levels across your servers and firewalls against a public vulnerability database. Summarize potential vulnerabilities per device in tabular form along with your mitigation plan for each.

subject: Password Crackability Assessment
body: An assessment reported that our passwords are easily cracked. Using a password-cracking tool and its default wordlist, validate this claim against a sample account on both a Linux host and the directory service. Report the fastest crack time observed for each, with screenshots showing the tool running.

subject: Web Page Integrity Monitoring
body: Peer organizations have reported website defacement. Implement a method (script or open-source tool) to monitor the integrity of your web content via hashing and alert if it changes unexpectedly. Document your approach with screenshots, including how alerts will reach your team.

subject: Password Policy - Design
body: Weak passwords have been a recurring problem. Draft a password policy for organization-wide use that specifies: minimum length and complexity (upper, lower, numeric, special character), account lockout after a defined number of failed attempts, a maximum password age, and a prohibition on password hints. Submit as a standalone policy document.

subject: Password Policy - Technical Implementation
body: Implement your previously-submitted password policy as a technical control across the directory service, the perimeter firewall, and all Linux hosts. Document, per system, which requirements were implemented, evidence of enforcement (e.g. a rejected weak password, a lockout after repeated failures), and any exceptions with justification.
deliverable_format: business memo with a compliance table and screenshots

subject: Account Lockout Policy
body: To reduce exposure to brute-force attacks, implement an account-lockout policy on all Windows and Linux systems. Document the configuration per system and provide evidence of a lockout occurring after repeated failed attempts.

subject: Create Departmental Directory Groups
body: Create directory (e.g. Active Directory) security groups for each major business department and correctly assign existing users to them, to support identity management and role-based access control going forward. Provide a screenshot showing the groups and their location within the directory structure.

subject: Harden Privileged and Service Accounts
body: Auditors flagged weak controls on our non-standard accounts. For service accounts, enable stronger complexity, enforce password history, and set a minimum and maximum password age with a longer minimum length. For domain/enterprise administrator accounts, rename default administrator and guest accounts, apply stricter password requirements, and deny interactive/RDP login to anything other than designated management systems. Group both account types for easier future management and document all changes.

subject: Urgent Bulk Account Provisioning
body: A new group of temporary staff starts shortly and needs accounts immediately. Provision login IDs, email addresses, and initial passwords for the listed users (see attached roster) within the requested time window, following your standard onboarding and password policy. Document completion with screenshots.

subject: Privileged User Audit Script
body: Audit is requesting a report on privileged directory accounts. Write a script (PowerShell or equivalent) that reports, for each privileged account: group membership, account creation date, last password change, and password expiration date. Submit the script alongside its output.

subject: Local Host Firewall Configuration
body: Enable and configure the local software firewall on every server (Windows and Linux) so only the expected inbound and outbound services are reachable, in both directions. Document the policy per host, with screenshots verifying the configuration.

subject: Endpoint Protection Deployment
body: Select and deploy an endpoint protection solution (commercial trial or open-source, e.g. ClamAV) so every host has baseline protection against malware and known attack signatures. Document your approach with screenshots showing the product installed and running on each host, particularly end-user workstations.

subject: File System Permissions and Auditing
body: Confidential documents on our servers require tighter file-system controls so unauthorized users cannot read them. Review and correct permissions on affected files/directories, and enable auditing so access and access attempts are logged. Confirm both changes are complete.
deliverable_format: business memo with permission and audit-log screenshots

subject: Harden IoT/Embedded Devices
body: Given the current threat level against IoT-class devices on our network, apply baseline hardening to any embedded/IoT systems: replace default administrative credentials with a new account, enable automatic security updates where supported, configure key-based (passphrase-protected) authentication for remote access, and enable a brute-force protection tool such as fail2ban for exposed services. Submit a memo with screenshots documenting each step.

subject: SSH Hardening on Linux Hosts
body: SSH is the only remote-access method authorized on Linux systems; legacy protocols such as Telnet or the r-commands are insecure and prohibited. For each Linux host: document which remote-access daemons are currently running, configure SSH for authorized users only with root login disabled (enable sudo for authorized admins), disable any other remote-access daemons, and apply a recognized SSH hardening guide (including disabling password authentication in favor of key pairs if the guide recommends it). Provide evidence per host.

subject: Switch Port Security Baseline
body: Implement baseline Layer 2 security on the LAN switch: shut down unused ports, lock single-host ports to their expected MAC address, and restrict VLANs/subnets to expected traffic only. Document the CLI commands used to implement each control.
deliverable_format: business memo with CLI configuration excerpts

subject: Rogue DHCP Server Defense
body: A neighboring organization recently suffered an outage caused by a rogue DHCP server on their network. Confirm whether your switching infrastructure supports DHCP snooping (or an equivalent protection) and enable it, noting whether any firmware/IOS upgrade is required. Document the exact configuration and your assessment.
deliverable_format: business memo with CLI configuration excerpts

subject: Credible Threat of Network Compromise
body: Law enforcement has indicated intelligence suggesting your network may be compromised, and a threat actor claims to have staged destructive malware set to trigger imminent unless certain demands are met. Leadership will not negotiate. Immediately launch a search for the described malware and activate your incident response plan. A file hash provided by investigators may be useful during your search. Submit an incident report within the stated deadline or scoring impact will apply.

subject: Suspected Data Breach - Customer Information
body: Customer records may have surfaced outside the organization. Verify whether a breach has occurred and, if so, prepare: a memo to the executive team summarizing what happened, a public-facing statement acknowledging the breach, and a direct notification to affected customers. Include any artifacts from your logs that help establish the scope of the exposure.
deliverable_format: incident memo plus public statement plus customer notice

subject: Media Coverage of Reported Breach
body: A previously suspected breach has now reached media coverage. Verify the details referenced in the reporting, then issue an updated memo to the executive board and a remedial press release addressing the specifics raised by the story.

subject: Shareholder and Customer Breach Inquiries
body: Following public rumors of a network compromise, shareholders and customers have begun sending inquiry letters. Draft a professional, individualized response letter following your incident response and data classification policies, ready for the Public Relations team to send, addressing the specific questions raised without over- or under-disclosing.

subject: Suspicious Email Triage
body: The help desk is fielding calls about a suspicious email (text provided in the attached ticket). Determine whether it is legitimate, assess whether any link it contains is dangerous and what would happen if a user visited it, and provide clear guidance the help desk can relay to concerned users. This is time-sensitive - the queue is backing up.

subject: Insider Threat Risk Assessment
body: Recent industry discussion has raised concern about the damage a malicious or careless insider could cause. Write a memo describing how your team would protect against insider threats and the potential impact if one occurred. Include a table of specific risk vectors (e.g. network access, removable media) with an estimate of potential impact for each.

subject: Investigate Suspicious Outbound Connections
body: There is concern that data exfiltration or backdoor access may be occurring. Use your firewall and centralized logs to identify suspicious outbound connections and take steps to mitigate any you find. Document your analysis process with screenshots, what was found, how it was mitigated, and your assessment of likely impact.

subject: Unauthorized Account Audit
body: There is reason to believe backdoor accounts may have been created following a suspected breach. Review access credentials across all systems and evaluate whether each account is legitimate. Document every device reviewed, any unauthorized accounts found, and the criteria used for your evaluation.

subject: Database-Backed Web Application Risk Briefing
body: Marketing is partnering with development on a new public-facing web application backed by a database. In terms a non-technical stakeholder can follow, explain the current risk landscape for this type of application (e.g. injection attacks), the relevant known vulnerability classes, and how to defend against them. Include a short incident-response outline specific to this application.

subject: Email Authentication Records (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
body: We continue to see fraudulent and spoofed email reaching the organization. Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records in DNS to reduce this exposure. Document the specific records you created, demonstrate they resolve correctly (e.g. via a DNS query tool), and briefly explain the benefits and limitations of each technology.

subject: Internal DNS Information Leak
body: It appears our DNS configuration is leaking internal address information to the public internet. Determine why and remediate it, while continuing to correctly serve DNS for public-facing systems. Provide a screenshot demonstrating that external DNS queries resolve public records but fail to resolve internal ones, along with a description of the technical fix.

subject: IPv6 Readiness and Addressing Plan
body: A key customer requires IPv6 connectivity going forward. Assess IPv6 readiness across routers, firewalls, switches, and servers, and develop a subnetting plan for your existing network segments (plus room for future segments) from the address block provided in your team packet. Cite the standards or references used in developing your addressing scheme, and present device readiness in tabular form.

subject: Urgent Credential Request for Auditors
body: A message arrives, purportedly from the CIO, written informally and with unusual urgency: auditors need every username and password across all systems immediately, in a single unencrypted plain-text file, or staff will face consequences. There is no verified channel confirming the sender's identity, and the request itself conflicts with standard security practice.
deliverable_format: judgment call - refusal/escalation memo expected, not credentials

subject: Colleague Requesting Workstation Access
body: An employee from another team reports they are running late for a video conference and asks to be given access to a colleague's workstation to join in time. Determine the appropriate way to handle this request in line with your access-control and physical-security policies, and document the outcome.
deliverable_format: judgment call - memo documenting the decision and rationale
